Environment: Research on the environmental interactions, pressures, impacts and management associated with salmon aquaculture.
Environment > General environmental issu: Broad environmental issues spanning multiple environmental topics where no single environmental pathway dominates.
Environment > Resource use and footprint: Environmental resource demands and footprints associated with salmon production, including marine resources, land, crops, water, energy and greenhouse-gas emissions.
Environment > Waste and emissions: Waste streams and emissions from salmon aquaculture, including nutrients, organic matter, chemicals, therapeutants, plastics and other solid waste.
Environment > Physical environment: Interactions between salmon aquaculture and the surrounding physical environment, including water flow, sediments, benthic conditions and water quality.
Environment > Escapes: Occurrence, prevention and consequences of farmed salmon escaping from aquaculture systems.
Environment > Wild populations and ecosy: Interactions and impacts involving wild populations, wildlife, biodiversity and ecosystem processes associated with salmon aquaculture.
Environment > Environmental stressors: Environmental conditions and natural hazards that affect farmed salmon, production performance, health, welfare or farm operations.
Environment > Climate change: Research on climate-change adaptation or mitigation in relation to salmon aquaculture.
Environment > Environmental management: Monitoring, assessment, mitigation, remediation and other management of environmental impacts from salmon aquaculture.
Industry and governance: Research on the structure, development, economics, markets, governance and regulation of the salmon aquaculture sector.
Industry and governance > Sector develop: Historical development, innovation and technological or organisational change across the salmon aquaculture sector.
Industry and governance > Firms and indu: Companies, ownership, concentration, investment and business strategy within the salmon aquaculture industry.
Industry and governance > Economics and: Economic costs, profitability, productivity, efficiency, risk, valuation and wider economic performance of salmon aquaculture.
Industry and governance > Markets, trade: Market dynamics, international trade, value and supply chains, retail, branding and marketing of farmed salmon.
Industry and governance > Governance and: Policy, law, regulation, licensing, spatial governance, standards, certification, compliance, enforcement and participation relating to salmon aquaculture.
Inputs and resources: Research on upstream resources, materials and other inputs required for salmon aquaculture, including feed resources, farm inputs and circular resource use.
Inputs and resources > Feed-resource sup: Production, sourcing, availability and supply of marine, crop-based and novel resources used in salmon feed.
Inputs and resources > Farm inputs: Availability, sourcing and provision of water, energy, therapeutants, chemicals, infrastructure and equipment required for salmon production.
Inputs and resources > Circularity: Circular use, recovery and efficiency of materials, nutrients, by-products and waste streams within salmon aquaculture and connected systems.
Methods: Research in which the principal contribution is a method, measurement approach, analytical technique, model, experimental design or evidence-synthesis method relevant to salmon aquaculture.
Methods > Methodological research: Development, validation, comparison or review of diagnostic, monitoring, measurement, modelling, experimental-design, classification or evidence-synthesis methods.
People and society: Research on the social, cultural, labour, livelihood, justice, food-security and public-health dimensions of salmon aquaculture.
People and society > General social issu: Broad social issues spanning multiple social topics where no single social pathway dominates.
People and society > Labour and employme: Employment, working conditions, occupational health, labour rights, exploitation and migration associated with salmon aquaculture.
People and society > Communities and liv: Effects of salmon aquaculture on livelihoods, income, local development, wellbeing, displacement, conflict and social licence.
People and society > Equity, justice and: Distributional equity, environmental justice, human rights and Indigenous peoples and rights in relation to salmon aquaculture.
People and society > Food security and a: Effects of salmon aquaculture and its resource demands on food availability, nutritional security, affordability, access and competition with other food uses.
People and society > Culture and knowled: Cultural meanings, identity, traditions, local and Indigenous knowledge, and public discourse or representation concerning salmon aquaculture.
People and society > Public health: Public-health implications of salmon aquaculture, including antimicrobial resistance, One Health and human-health effects arising from farming activities.
Product: Research on the composition, quality, processing, safety, nutrition, health effects, consumption and consumer attributes of farmed salmon products.
Product > General product issues: Broad product issues spanning multiple attributes where no single product characteristic dominates.
Product > Composition and nutritional va: Nutritional composition, contaminants and residues in harvested salmon products.
Product > Fillet and carcass quality: Physical, visual and compositional quality of salmon fillets and carcasses, including product yield.
Product > Sensory quality: Taste, flavour, odour, aroma, mouthfeel and other sensory properties or acceptability of salmon products.
Product > Processing and preservation: Post-harvest processing, value addition, storage, packaging, preservation and shelf life of salmon products.
Product > Food safety: Microbiological and chemical hazards affecting the safety of salmon as a food product.
Product > Human nutrition and health: Human nutritional benefits, risks and physiological outcomes associated with consuming salmon.
Product > Consumers and consumption: Consumption patterns, preferences, purchasing choices, willingness to pay, perceptions, knowledge, trust and responses to labels or product origin.
Production: Research on the biological, technical and operational processes used to produce farmed salmon, including health, welfare, nutrition, husbandry, production systems and harvest.
Production > Fish health: Health and disease of farmed salmon, including sea lice, infectious and non-infectious diseases, epidemiology, diagnosis, prevention, treatment and host responses.
Production > Fish welfare: Assessment, risks, consequences and improvement of welfare in farmed salmon.
Production > Breeding and reproduction: Selective breeding, genetic improvement, broodstock management, reproductive performance, maturation and sterility control in farmed salmon.
Production > Early life and transfer: Production and management of eggs, fry, parr and smolts, including smoltification and transfer to seawater.
Production > Feed and nutrition: Feed ingredients, additives, nutrient requirements, formulation, feeding strategies, digestibility, nutrient utilisation and feed efficiency in farmed salmon.
Production > Husbandry and farm manageme: Farm-level husbandry and management practices including stocking density, handling, grading, transport, environmental control and biosecurity.
Production > Production systems and tech: Design, operation and performance of salmon production systems and technologies, including cages, land-based systems, RAS, offshore systems, integrated aquaculture and automation.
Production > Fish performance and biolog: Growth, development, physiology, metabolism, anatomy, tissues and behaviour of farmed salmon where these are substantive production-related outcomes.
Production > Stress and mortality: Causes, responses and consequences of stress, mortality and survival loss in farmed salmon.
Production > Harvest and slaughter: Harvest, pre-slaughter management, stunning and slaughter of farmed salmon, including operational and welfare consequences.
